objective: Add HTTP validators to encrypted media responses, remove container healthcheck noise from the request log, emit non-identifying media read observations, and add previous-secret support so encryption keys can be rotated at all. Also repair the stale test fixtures and mocks that leave the suite red on main, so the release gate can run.
userOutcome: Repeat views of a photo revalidate instead of re-downloading and re-decrypting, retained API logs cover about a day and a half of real traffic instead of eight hours of healthchecks, and a leaked media, message, feed or profile key can be replaced without destroying the data already encrypted under it.
audience: Authenticated cruush members viewing profile, message and feed photos, and Julien operating the production box.
successCriteria: Media responses carry a strong ETag derived from the stored object key and its wrapping key version.
A request whose If-None-Match matches receives 304 with no body and without reading or decrypting the stored object.
Authentication and per-surface authorization still run on every media request, including revalidations.
GET /health still returns 200 and the container healthcheck is unchanged, but neither is written to the request log.
A value sealed before a rotation still decrypts once the outgoing secret is retained as the previous one.
With no previous secret configured, encryption behaviour is identical to before the change.
server typecheck passes and the crypto, media and content test files pass.
Rotation is available for media, message, feed, profile, location, visibility policy, ghost and relationship data.
Test fixtures and mocks that drifted from the code are repaired, without weakening or deleting any assertion.
mustPreserve: Every media route authenticates before any authorization or observation work.
Per-surface authorization: block checks for profile photos, conversation membership plus view-once and expiry for message photos, feed access for feed photos.
Envelope encryption of media bytes at rest and the moderation-approved and not-deleted row filters.
The Docker healthcheck definition and the /health route body.
Fastify's existing request log line shapes for every non-healthcheck request.
Decryption of every value already sealed under the current secrets.
Every existing test assertion. Fixtures may gain fields the code genuinely returns; no assertion may be relaxed or removed to make a run pass.
nonGoals: Rate limiting media reads. That is a later phase and depends on measurement.
Rotation for index keys and stored token hashes, which cannot use a previous-secret fallback.
Any robots, indexing or marketing surface change.
Rotation for index keys and stored token hashes (relationship-index, match-token-signing, profile-token, display-session), which are compared by hash and cannot use a previous-secret fallback.

assumptions.statement: Encrypted media bytes behind a given object key are never rewritten, so the object key plus its wrapping key version is a stable strong validator.
assumptions.impact: If bytes were rewritten in place under the same key, a stale cached body could be served until the version changed.

assumptions.statement: private, no-cache is preferred over a long max-age so blocks, deletions and withdrawn moderation approvals revoke immediately.
assumptions.impact: Costs one conditional request per view instead of serving from cache silently, in exchange for immediate revocation.

assumptions.statement: Salting read observations with the UTC day gives exact within-day counts without recording which member viewed whose photo.
assumptions.impact: Counts cannot be linked across day boundaries, which is acceptable for choosing a daily budget.

nextVisibleMilestone: Media responses revalidate with 304 instead of re-sending bodies, production logs stop being 81 percent healthcheck, and media, message, feed and profile keys become rotatable.
stopConditions: Any media route would answer without authenticating.
Any test that passed on origin/main starts failing.
A change would make already-encrypted data unreadable.
A change would require touching production applications or secrets.
publicationTarget: local branch feat/media-read-rate-limit; commit only, no push or deploy
requiredEvidence: npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit in server exits 0 with zero errors.
npx vitest run src/key-rotation.test.ts passes, including the case proving decryption fails closed when the outgoing secret is not retained.
npx vitest run src/media-read-validator.test.ts passes, including that a 304 is returned without reading the stored object and that authentication is still required.
The 20 crypto, media, content and config test files pass with 90 tests and no failures.
app.test.ts and profile-schema.test.ts failures were reproduced on a stashed tree, so they pre-exist on origin/main.
src/key-rotation.test.ts covers media, message and feed round trips across a rotation, each with a fails-closed case.
